data.personality: Cheerful, stubborn and endlessly hungry. You don't leave family out on the tide.
data.bonds: Grandson of Old Cobb, one of the missing fishermen. Afraid of deep water, though he'd never admit it.
data.backstory: Pip learned to read the tides, the weather and the birds from his grandfather. He knows every gully on the mudflats and every rock on the causeway - and he knows Old Cobb would never have walked out to the lighthouse on his own.
data.dmSecrets: Old Cobb did not go willingly; he saw the cult drown the lighthouse keeper forty years ago and has kept silent ever since.
data.name: Pip Cobble
data.description: Halfling ranger and tide-reader, out to bring his grandfather Old Cobb home.

data.personality: Precise, curious and a little too pleased when she is right. Knowledge drowned is knowledge stolen.
data.bonds: Has spent three years reconstructing the lost parish records of Old Saltmere. Will take terrible risks for a primary source.
data.backstory: A scholar from the university at Carrow, Isolde came to Saltmere to map the drowned town before the sea takes the last of it. The low tide is the chance of a lifetime - and the green light is a mystery she cannot leave alone.
data.dmSecrets: Her great-grandmother was the last lighthouse keeper's wife. Mother Brine knows, and has been very kind to her.
data.name: Isolde Marrow
data.description: Half-elf diviner and antiquarian, in Saltmere to map the drowned town while the tide is out.

data.personality: Patient, gruff and kind. Every soul deserves a light to steer by.
data.bonds: His younger brother Jory is one of the missing fishermen. He blames himself for not coming home sooner.
data.backstory: Aldous left Saltmere at sixteen to serve in the chapel of the Harbour Keeper, a small god of safe returns. He came home on the morning coach to find his brother's boat beached on the mud and his brother gone.
data.dmSecrets: Jory is still alive in the lighthouse - but he has started to wear the shell token willingly.
data.name: Brother Aldous Penhale
data.description: Dwarf cleric of the Harbour Keeper, home to find his brother Jory among the missing.

data.personality: Quick, cheerful and impossible to keep in one place. Believes nobody should drown for someone else's profit.
data.bonds: Owes Harbourmaster Vell for keeping her out of the stocks. Can't resist climbing anything tall - including lighthouses.
data.backstory: Wren grew up in the rigging of smugglers' cutters running brandy past Saltmere. When her last ship went down she washed ashore with nothing but a knife and a debt. She has worked the quays ever since, and Jory Penhale was the only fisherman who never cheated her.
data.dmSecrets: Wren once carried a sealed crate for Mother Brine across the causeway at low tide. It was heavy, wet and humming.
data.name: Wren Halloway
data.description: Human rogue and former smuggler's rigger. Quick hands, quicker grin, and a debt to the harbourmaster.

data.role: High priestess of the Children of the Tide; runs the salting house
data.voice: Wet, patient whisper. Smells of brine. Ends sentences with 'as the tide wills'. Never blinks first.
data.secrets: She drowned the lighthouse keeper to wake the Lantern. Believes the drowned town of Old Saltmere can be raised if the light shines on the night of the black tide.
data.name: Mother Brine
data.description: Kindly old salt-wife who feeds stray cats. Secretly leads the tide cult.

data.role: Harbourmaster of Saltmere; keeps the boat register and the town purse
data.voice: Slow, heavy voice. Taps the ledger when he is worried. Calls everyone “friend” and means it.
data.name: Harbourmaster Osric Vell
data.description: Tired, honest harbourmaster offering 50 gp for the three missing fishermen.

data.role: Serves tables at the Gull and Anchor; daughter of the missing Wat Trebarra
data.voice: Quick, blunt and furious. Never sits down. Spins her father’s shell token between her fingers.
data.name: Tilly Gorse
data.description: Fierce fourteen-year-old barmaid who found a cult token in her missing father’s coat.

data.readAloud: Saltmere smells of tar and old fish. Slate roofs climb the cliff above a harbour that is no longer a harbour: the sea has drawn back half a mile, and every boat in town lies tilted on the black mud. Far out across the flats, the old lighthouse leans against the sky.
data.name: Saltmere
data.description: A hard little fishing town on a grey northern coast, half of it drowned forty years ago.

data.readAloud: Low beams, a smoking hearth and a ship’s figurehead glaring down over the bar. Talk stops when strangers come in. In the corner, three tankards stand full and untouched on an empty table.
data.name: The Gull and Anchor
data.description: The fishermen’s tavern on the quay, where the three missing men drank their last.

data.readAloud: The tide is out, and for the first time in forty years the causeway stands bare. At its end the lighthouse leans like a drunk, barnacled to the gallery rail - and at its top, impossibly, a green light is burning.
data.name: The Drowned Lighthouse

data.properties:
Requires attunement by a creature that has drowned and returned.
The Lantern's lens is a great green sea-glass eye salvaged from Old Saltmere's church. Lit, it sheds dim green light in a 120-foot cone. Water in the cone recedes from the shore for as long as the light burns.
The Black Tide. On the night of the black tide, a creature attuned to the Lantern can shine it on drowned ground and speak the names of the dead buried there. Each named creature rises as a drowned acolyte loyal to the bearer.
Curse. Each dawn the bearer must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or walk into the sea at the next high tide.
data.name: The Drowned Lantern
data.description: The green-glass lantern at the top of the lighthouse. It shines into the past - and the past is waking up.

data.goals:
Raise drowned Old Saltmere on the night of the black tide.
- Recruit the desperate with the promise of lost family returned.
- Mark members with a carved spiral shell token.
- Drown those who refuse, and bring them back as acolytes.
data.name: Children of the Tide
data.description: A secret sea cult that worships the tide and serves Mother Brine.

schema.description: Guilds, cults, noble houses and other organisations.

data.traits:
Amphibious. The acolyte can breathe air and water.
Tide-Touched. While standing in water, the acolyte has advantage on saving throws against being knocked prone.
data.actions:
Gaff Hook. Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 11).
Drown (Recharge 5-6). One creature grappled by the acolyte must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw or take 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage as seawater fills its lungs.
data.name: Drowned Acolyte

data.summary: Jory Penhale, Wat Trebarra and Old Cobb went drinking at the Gull and Anchor three nights ago and never came home. All three wore the shell token of the Children of the Tide. Their boats are still beached on the mud. Harbourmaster Osric Vell will pay 50 gold pieces to anyone who brings them back - alive, or at least accounted for.
data.name: The Missing Fishermen
data.description: Three fishermen vanished the night the tide went out. Find them before the black tide.
